question_en: When a commodity has very little or no convenience yield, the futures market is said to be in:
explanation_en: When there is little or no convenience yield, futures markets are most likely in contango, a situation where futures prices are higher than spot prices. Backwardation refers a market where futures prices are less than spot prices and is associated with a high convenience yield. The no-arbitrage condition is what theoretically drives the relationship between spot commodity prices and futures prices.

question_en: The covariance of monthly returns for two stocks is 0.91. Based on the covariance, it is most accurate to conclude that the monthly returns on these two stocks have:
explanation_en: Covariance indicates the direction of the linear relationship (i.e., positive or negative) between two variables, but its magnitude does not directly indicate the strength of that relationship. If 0.91 was the correlation, rather than the covariance, it would indicate the monthly returns on these two stocks have a strong linear relationship.

question_en: Which of the following statements regarding the differences between interest rate swaps and forward rate agreements is most accurate?
option_a: Forward rate agreements are commitments, whereas interest rate swaps are contingent claims.
option_b: Forward rate agreements have a single settlement date, whereas interest rate swaps have several settlement dates.
option_c: Ignoring transactions costs, forward rate agreements require no upfront payment, whereas interest rate swaps require the payment of an upfront premium.
explanation_en: Interest rate swaps settle periodically during their tenor, whereas an FRA settles only once, at maturity. Both are forward commitments and neither requires an upfront payment.

question_en: A clawback provision is most likely to be included in the partnership agreement of an alternative investment fund that has:
explanation_en: With a deal-by-deal waterfall structure, if successful deals that generate gains are exited early in a fund's life and unsuccessful deals that generate losses are exited later, it is possible that incentive fees exceed the agreed-upon percentage of gains over the fund's life. With a clawback provision, the general partner is required to return any excess incentive fees to the limited partners.

question_en: In securitization, the party that purchases the loans is least likely:
explanation_en: The issuer purchases the loans or other financial securities and issues the asset- backed securities. The issuer is created as a special purpose entity. Often, the originator of the loans also services the loans.

question_en:
An index is composed of the following three stocks:

| Stock | Dec 31, 20X1 Price | Dec 31, 20X1 Shares | Dec 31, 20X2 Price | Dec 31, 20X2 Shares |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Perez | $140 | 1,000,000 | $154 | 1,000,000 |
| Quinton | $70 | 1,500,000 | $70 | 2,000,000 |
| Ranovich | $90 | 2,000,000 | $81 | 2,000,000 |

An equal-weighted index of the three stocks has a value on December 31, 20X1 = 100. The index value on December 31, 20X2 is closest to:
explanation_en: Percentage price changes were +10% for Perez, 0% for Quinton, and −10% for Ranovich. The change in an equal-weighted index is (10% + 0% −10%) / 3 = 0% and the index value remains equal to 100.

question_en: Consider an investor who writes a put on a share at X for premium of $5 and an investor who takes a long forward position at X in the same asset for the same period. If ST is the asset price at settlement, both investors will have the same profit at settlement only if:
explanation_en: The profit on the put is 5 – Max(0, X – ST) and the profit on the forward is ST – X . When the put expires out of the money, X < ST, the profit on the short put is 5 (put expires worthless) and the payoff at settlement on the forward position is positive. When ST = X + 5, both positions have a profit of 5.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 6 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Berg AB, a Swedish company, had at the end of the last accounting period DTLs of SEK 30 million and DTAs of SEK 12 million. During the current period, the authorities raised the tax rate from 30% to 35%. The impact on Berg's tax expense due to the adjustment of existing DTAs and DTLs at the time of the change will:
option_c: have no impact on tax expense.
explanation_en: The increase in the tax rate will increase both the DTLs and the DTAs. Because the DTLs are larger, they will have a greater effect on tax expense. Using the relationship that tax expense = tax payable + ΔDTL – ΔDTA, and knowing the DTLs will increase by more than the DTAs, the net impact of the changes is to increase tax expense.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 6 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following would most likely lead to a company having little pricing power?
option_a: High xed costs and high exit barriers.
option_b: Many suppliers and low switching costs for production inputs.
option_c: Small number of customers in the market and high switching costs for the product.
explanation_en: High fixed costs and exit barriers both increase industry rivalry. With increased competition, pricing power is lower. A small number of customers in the market increases the bargaining power of each customer, which may indicate lower pricing power, although their bargaining power might be less if switching costs for the product are high. Many suppliers and low switching costs for production inputs reduce the bargaining power of suppliers. This has a direct impact on the company's costs, but not on its pricing power.

question_en: A member is hired to write a research report on a company that is paid for by the company with a flat fee and fixed bonus if the firm's shares become more widely held. The member is:
option_a: not in violation of the Standards as long as the fact that the research is issuer- funded is disclosed.
option_b: not in violation of the Standards as long as both the source of the funding and the nature of the compensation is disclosed.
option_c: in violation of the Standards even if both the funding source and the nature of the compensation are disclosed.
explanation_en: According to Standard I(B) Independence and Objectivity, the member would be in violation because the nature of the compensation can be reasonably expected to influence the member's independence and objectivity.

question_en: Geopolitical risks are characterized as "black swan" risks if they have a:
explanation_en: Black swan risk refers to an unanticipated event with low likelihood (e.g., a pandemic or war) that would have a substantial short-term impact.

question_en: Joey Balder, CFA, an employee of Flagship Investment Managers, is offered a position as Flagship's Southtown branch supervisor. Balder is reluctant to accept the position because certain compliance procedures have not been adopted in that branch. To comply with the Standards, Balder should most appropriately:
option_a: accept the position on condition that his concerns will be addressed.
option_b: decline in writing to accept the supervisory position until the firm adopts appropriate procedures.
option_c: discuss his concerns with management and not accept the position unless and until he is given authority over compliance procedures.
explanation_en: Standard IV(C) Responsibilities of Supervisors requires that if a member cannot discharge compliance responsibilities because of a poor compliance system, the member should decline in writing to accept supervisory responsibility until the firm adopts an adequate system.

question_en: An investor would like to limit his exposure to adverse events associated with environmental, social, and governance risks. Which of the following investments in a company's securities is best suited for this purpose?
explanation_en: Although equity holders face the most ESG risk, long-term debt investors face more ESG risk than short-term debt investors.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 6 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Forecasting future earnings of a company based on whether it changes its main supplier is best described as an example of:
explanation_en: Scenario analysis is based on specific alternatives, such as the impact changing a supplier will have on earnings. Sensitivity analysis is based on "what if" questions such as "what will be the effect on net income if sales increase by 3% rather than the estimated 5%". Sensitivity analysis does not specifically consider what has caused sales to increase or the likelihood of this happening. Simulation is a technique in which probability distributions for key variables are selected and a computer is then used to generate a distribution of values for outcomes.

question_en: One week after taking the Level II CFA exam, Mindy Hauser posts a message on a popular Web site: "I do not believe CFA Institute tested the curriculum fairly. I was ready to use the trick I learned for triangular arbitrage problems, and there weren't any on the exam." Does Hauser's message violate the Standards related to conduct as a CFA candidate?
option_a: No, because expressing an opinion is not a violation.
option_b: Yes, because it compromises the reputation of the CFA Institute.
option_c: Yes, because it compromises the integrity of the CFA examinations.
explanation_en: Standard VII(A) Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs prohibits candidates from revealing information about the content of the CFA exams, including which topic areas or formulas were, or were not, tested on an exam.

question_en: A company's pretax cost of debt is 7% and its cost of equity is 9%. With a 20% tax rate and a capital structure that has twice as much debt as equity, the company's weighted-average cost of capital is closest to:
explanation_en: A capital structure with twice as much debt as equity has two-thirds debt and one- third equity. The after-tax cost of debt is 7% × (1 – 0.20) = 5.6%. WACC = 2/3 × 5.6% + 1/3 × 9% = 3.73% + 3% = 6.73%.

question_en: Which of the following actions by a company's management or board of directors is most likely to represent a principal-agent conflict?
option_a: Implementing a dual-class voting structure for common shares.
option_b: Increasing the size of the company with an unnecessary acquisition.
option_c: Issuing new debt while increasing dividends to common shareholders.
explanation_en: Principal-agent conflicts are those between shareholders (as principals) and management and the board of directors (as agents). An example of an action that may represent a principal-agent conflict is "empire building" that results from management compensation structures that are tied to the size of the firm, rather than being better aligned with shareholders' interests. Issuing new debt while increasing dividends to common shareholders represents a conflict between shareholders' interests and creditors' interests. Dual-class structures may create conflicts among different groups of shareholders.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 6 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements regarding record retention is most accurate?
option_a: The Standards require that records be retained for a minimum of seven years.
option_b: While members are responsible for retaining research notes and other supporting documents, record retention is generally the responsibility of the firm.
option_c: When a member changes employers, the member is responsible for transferring the records supporting his recommendations to his new employer.
explanation_en: The firm is generally responsible for record-keeping as required by Standard V(C) Record Retention. Retaining records for at least seven years is not required by the Standard but is recommended if no other regulation applies. Records supporting investment actions and recommendations are the property of the firm. A member cannot take these records or copies of them to a new employer without permission from the original employer.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 6 - Answers.pdf
question_en: A country implementing a tariff on imports is most likely to have a negative economic effect on:
explanation_en: By increasing the domestic price of imported goods, a tariff harms foreign exporters by decreasing demand for their goods, and harms domestic consumers by increasing the price of goods they otherwise prefer. A tariff benefits domestic producers by encouraging consumers to substitute away from imports and toward domestic goods. The domestic government also benefits by collecting the tariff revenue.

question_en: To estimate the standard error of the sample mean using jackknife resampling, an analyst should remove how many of the observations from each sample?
explanation_en: Jackknife resampling involves calculating multiple sample means, each with one of the observations removed from the sample, and using the standard deviation of these sample means as an estimate of the standard error of the sample mean.
